cases.title: Plant contact dermatitis, new patient

sections.heading: Chief complaint
sections.text: Itchy rash on both forearms for 2 days.

sections.heading: History of present illness
sections.text: 34-year-old woman, new to the practice, seen in the walk-in session. She pulled weeds along her back fence 3 days ago and the next morning noticed itchy red streaks with a few small blisters on both forearms. No rash on the face or elsewhere. No fever, no eye swelling, no trouble breathing. She has not tried any treatment and prefers to avoid medicines if possible. No similar rash before. Her primary care clinician practices elsewhere.

sections.heading: Review of systems
sections.text: Positive for itching. Negative for fever, facial swelling, shortness of breath and joint pain.

sections.heading: Physical exam
sections.text: Well appearing. Skin: linear erythematous papules and scattered 1 to 2 mm vesicles in streaks on the volar forearms bilaterally, about 4% of body surface area. No pustules, crusting or warmth. Face, eyelids and lips normal.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Allergic contact dermatitis due to poison ivy, both forearms, localized. Cool compresses 3 times a day and colloidal oatmeal baths. No medication, at her preference. Wash the gloves and clothing worn while weeding. Expected to clear in 1 to 3 weeks. Return if the rash spreads to the face, blisters become large, or there are signs of infection.

rationale.level: MDM straightforward. Problems: one self-limited problem (localized plant contact dermatitis). Data: none. Risk: minimal (cool compresses and oatmeal baths, no medication). Data and risk are both minimal, so 99202 holds even if the problem were read as acute uncomplicated (low).

codes.L23.7: Allergic contact dermatitis due to plants, except food: poison ivy named in the assessment.

rationale.billing: Billed 99203 (low MDM). With minimal data and minimal risk low MDM cannot be met: one level too high.
